Missouri Tigers.career_experience: Won the Ole Miss starting job over Trinidad Chambliss and started the first two games of 2025 before injury.
Missouri Tigers.previous_starts: Two — the first two games of 2025 at Ole Miss.
Missouri Tigers.passing: Not addressed in guide as a yardage or touchdown line; the guide reports 84 dropbacks.
Missouri Tigers.efficiency: Not addressed in guide as a completion rate.
Missouri Tigers.turnovers: Five interceptions on 84 dropbacks and a 5.7% turnover-worthy play rate — the guide's stated caveat on him.
Missouri Tigers.competition: None described — Simmons is presented as the incoming starter.
Missouri Tigers.author_confidence: Positive but explicitly conditional. The guide says that if he stops putting the ball in danger he could be one of the best portal pickups anywhere.
Missouri Tigers.positive_case: He did not lose the Ole Miss job on performance but through injury, which the guide stresses makes his availability unusual; he has a strong run game to lean on.
Missouri Tigers.concerns: Ball security is the single named caveat — five interceptions on 84 dropbacks at a 5.7% turnover-worthy play rate.
Missouri Tigers.supporting_cast: Strong. Ahmad Hardy and Jamal Roberts combined for 2,402 rushing yards and 22 touchdowns; Hardy alone ran for 1,649, forced 97 missed tackles and averaged 4.6 yards after contact, and though he suffered a gunshot wound in May the guide says he will be ready for fall camp. They run behind a line returning left tackle Cayden Green with 118 career starts in the room.
Missouri Tigers.portal_context: Simmons is the headline portal addition; the guide asks directly whether he could be the steal of the transfer portal.
Missouri Tigers.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 6.5 wins, stated as conditional on Simmons showing the qualities that won him the Ole Miss job over Chambliss and cutting out mistakes. The guide finds it hard to believe an offense of this caliber wins six or fewer.
Missouri Tigers.outlook_dependency: High. The guide attaches its Over explicitly to Simmons' performance and ball security, while noting the rushing attack is the offense's backbone.
Missouri Tigers.conflicts: The team spread prints total 12 returning starters with offense 9 and defense 6 (p. 300); offense plus defense is 15, which does not equal the printed total. All three figures are reproduced as printed in the Team Database and none is corrected here. This bears on any returning-starter reading of the quarterback position.

Oklahoma Sooners.previous_school: Washington State — the guide repeatedly benchmarks him against his final season there.
Oklahoma Sooners.career_experience: Established starter; the guide contrasts his Washington State form with his 2025 Oklahoma season.
Oklahoma Sooners.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count; the guide splits 2025 into a four-game and an eight-game stretch.
Oklahoma Sooners.passing: First four games of 2025: 67.6% at 8.5 yards per attempt with six touchdowns to three interceptions, at an 8.5-yard average depth of target. After breaking his throwing hand against Auburn, over the next eight games: 58.8% at 6.4 yards per attempt with eight touchdowns and eight interceptions.
Oklahoma Sooners.rushing: 565 rushing yards in 2025 on only 15 fewer carries than his final Washington State season, when he gained 1,008 yards and 15 touchdowns at 6.8 per attempt.
Oklahoma Sooners.efficiency: 67.6% then 58.8% completions; 8.5 then 6.4 yards per attempt; 8.5-yard average depth of target in the healthy stretch.
Oklahoma Sooners.turnovers: Three interceptions in the first four games, eight in the next eight. His 16 turnover-worthy plays across those eight games were third-most among SEC quarterbacks — and the guide refuses to attribute the decline solely to the injury.
Oklahoma Sooners.competition: None described — Mateer is the established starter.
Oklahoma Sooners.author_confidence: Guarded. The guide's conclusion is that he needs to be healthy and also better with the ball, and that he must improve in both passing and running.
Oklahoma Sooners.positive_case: His pre-injury form — 67.6% at 8.5 yards per attempt — plus a reunion with coordinator Ben Arbuckle, his coordinator at Washington State.
Oklahoma Sooners.concerns: The post-injury collapse in accuracy and yards per attempt, a turnover-worthy play count third-most in the SEC, and a rushing contribution far below his Washington State level.
Oklahoma Sooners.scheme_fit: Reunited with Ben Arbuckle, his Washington State coordinator, who the guide says has to fix both the passing decline and the run game.
Oklahoma Sooners.supporting_cast: Weak on the ground: 3.5 yards per carry team-wide, Tory Blaylock leading with 480 yards on 120 attempts, and finishes of 127th in rushing EPA per play and 128th in success rate. The guide credits new offensive linemen but says better play-calling is needed too.
Oklahoma Sooners.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 7.5 wins. The guide's logic is that if the defense is close to its 2025 level — which it expects — the win floor is very high, leaving the offense as the open question. Oklahoma must win one or two of Michigan, Georgia, Ole Miss, Texas A&M or Texas, and the guide rates the team good enough to do so.
Oklahoma Sooners.outlook_dependency: Very high. The season is framed as resting on Mateer and the offense, with the defense treated as the reliable half.
Oklahoma Sooners.conflicts: On conditioning the guide reports only what Mateer said — he appeared bulkier at the Manning Passing Academy and told media he had not gained weight but gotten in better shape. The guide does not resolve this and neither does this record.

Ole Miss Rebels.status: Returning starter — took the job during 2025 through Austin Simmons' injury and never gave it back.
Ole Miss Rebels.career_experience: Finished 2025 as PFF's third-highest graded SEC passer.
Ole Miss Rebels.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count; he took over during 2025 and held the job.
Ole Miss Rebels.passing: 65.6% completions, 8.8 yards per attempt, 22 touchdowns to three interceptions.
Ole Miss Rebels.efficiency: 65.6% completions at 8.8 yards per attempt; PFF's third-highest graded SEC passer.
Ole Miss Rebels.turnovers: Three interceptions, and a 2.5% turnover-worthy play rate — third-best among SEC starters, which the guide highlights as the contrast with Simmons.
Ole Miss Rebels.competition: None — the guide calls him the unquestioned starter entering 2026.
Ole Miss Rebels.author_confidence: High on the player. He is called the unquestioned starter and a Heisman candidate; the guide's doubts sit elsewhere on this team.
Ole Miss Rebels.positive_case: Elite 2025 production with outstanding ball security, retained as the settled starter.
Ole Miss Rebels.concerns: Whether he can repeat it amid heavy turnover in the receiver room — all four top receivers from 2025 are gone via draft, portal or otherwise — and a new offensive system around him.
Ole Miss Rebels.scheme_fit: Uncertain by construction. Offensive coordinator Charlie Weis Jr., described as central to the offense, has gone to Baton Rouge; John David Baker, East Carolina's coordinator in 2025, replaces him. The guide flags new terminology and unknown play structure and flow.
Ole Miss Rebels.supporting_cast: All four top receivers from 2025 are gone. Kewan Lacy remains a major piece in the backfield, but the guide warns of a possible large shift in the unit's efficiency.
Ole Miss Rebels.portal_context: Receiver is named among the groups Pete Golding has had to rebuild.
Ole Miss Rebels.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 7.5 wins. The quarterback is not the stated reason — the guide argues the departures matter more than the 16 returning starters: the architects of one of the country's better offenses, plus key pieces on both lines, combined with doubts about Golding and a taxing schedule.
Ole Miss Rebels.outlook_dependency: Moderate. Chambliss is treated as a settled strength; the guide's Under is argued from coaching departures, line losses and schedule rather than from quarterback risk. The QB-side risk it does name is the receiver turnover around him.

South Carolina Gamecocks.career_experience: Established starter across 2024 and 2025, which the guide compares directly.
South Carolina Gamecocks.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count.
South Carolina Gamecocks.passing: Completions fell from 64.8% in 2024 to 59.8% in 2025, with five fewer touchdown passes on only five fewer attempts. From a clean pocket: 67.3% for 9.3 yards per attempt with eight touchdowns and five interceptions, against 71.0% for 8.7 yards with 14 touchdowns and two interceptions the year before.
South Carolina Gamecocks.rushing: The running element fell away — 49 designed carries against 79 in 2024 — even though the underlying quality held: 4.64 yards after contact, 25 runs of 10-plus yards and 5.3 yards per attempt, all in line with the prior year.
South Carolina Gamecocks.efficiency: 59.8% overall, 67.3% from a clean pocket at 9.3 yards per attempt.
South Carolina Gamecocks.turnovers: Five interceptions from a clean pocket in 2025 against two the year before.
South Carolina Gamecocks.competition: None described — Sellers is the settled starter.
South Carolina Gamecocks.author_confidence: Openly doubtful. The guide calls the decline stark and says he must return to 2024 form to justify the hype, listing “whether Sellers' regression is real” as its first stacked doubt.
South Carolina Gamecocks.positive_case: He is described as a talented and very talented quarterback whose designed-run quality held up, joined by a play-caller with a record of maximizing quarterbacks.
South Carolina Gamecocks.concerns: A stark year-over-year passing decline, including from a clean pocket, and a running element that was used far less.
South Carolina Gamecocks.scheme_fit: New play-caller Kendal Briles has a long record of good offenses and of maximizing quarterbacks; the guide is genuinely curious how he uses Sellers and says he must fix the passing and use the skill set better.
South Carolina Gamecocks.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 6.5 wins, with the guide noting six wins still reaches a bowl. Its doubts are stacked explicitly as questions — whether Sellers' regression is real, whether Briles can restore his 2024 form, and how the offense measures against a slate of defenses ranking among the nation's best.
South Carolina Gamecocks.outlook_dependency: Very high. Sellers is identified as a main reason the offense declined, and his regression heads the list of doubts behind the Under.

Tennessee Volunteers.career_experience: True freshman; a five-star and the third-ranked member of the 2026 class.
Tennessee Volunteers.passing: High school only: threw one interception per 98 attempts.
Tennessee Volunteers.turnovers: High school only: one interception per 98 attempts.
Tennessee Volunteers.competition: Live. The guide records that Heupel insists Brandon is in a genuine battle with redshirt freshman George McIntyre, while noting the expectation is Brandon takes over full-time after the Furman opener, in which both are likely to play.
Tennessee Volunteers.author_confidence: Deliberately measured. The guide anticipates freshman growing pains, frames the move as about the programme's future, and hopes Brandon is the first multi-year answer after Heupel started a different quarterback in Week 1 of every season at Knoxville.
Tennessee Volunteers.positive_case: A five-star, third-ranked in his class, with exceptional high-school ball security, entering a system the guide calls user-friendly with a high floor.
Tennessee Volunteers.concerns: A true freshman starter threatens Tennessee's streak of at least 31.8 points per game every season under Heupel; the guide anticipates growing pains.
Tennessee Volunteers.scheme_fit: Explicitly favourable — the guide stresses the system is user-friendly and that annual quarterback churn has not disrupted a system with a high floor, with Heupel rated an elite play-caller.
Tennessee Volunteers.supporting_cast: Good enough to protect the scoring streak in the guide's judgement: an offensive line that lost one starter and is a Joe Moore Award contender, three of the top four receivers back outside leading receiver Chris Brazzell, and leading rusher DeSean Bishop returning.
Tennessee Volunteers.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 7.5 wins, resting on Heupel's consistency — at least eight wins in four straight years — plus immense offensive talent giving a firm floor despite the quarterback question. The guide calls eight wins likely but a sweat, and rates Tennessee a sneaky team with more upside than most expect if the true freshman hits.
Tennessee Volunteers.outlook_dependency: High on upside, lower on floor. The guide explicitly argues the floor holds despite the quarterback question, while making the upside case conditional on the freshman hitting.
Tennessee Volunteers.conflicts: Heupel is reported insisting on a genuine battle while the guide simultaneously states the expectation that Brandon takes over full-time after the opener. Both are recorded; neither is resolved.

Texas A&M Aggies.career_experience: Established starter; ranked 12th among SEC passers by PFF grade in 2025.
Texas A&M Aggies.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count.
Texas A&M Aggies.passing: 61.6% at 8.3 yards per attempt with 25 touchdowns to 12 interceptions. On throws of 10-19 yards between the numbers he completed 50.8% with six touchdowns and five interceptions.
Texas A&M Aggies.efficiency: 61.6% completions at 8.3 yards per attempt; 12th among SEC passers by PFF grade.
Texas A&M Aggies.turnovers: 12 interceptions; the third-highest turnover-worthy play rate in the conference at 4.7%, and a conference-leading 22 such plays, nine of them on 10-19 yard throws between the numbers.
Texas A&M Aggies.competition: None described — Reed is the settled starter.
Texas A&M Aggies.author_confidence: Qualified. The guide calls his production solid but argues it is insufficient for the next step, and says he has not shown real progress in his weak areas.
Texas A&M Aggies.positive_case: Solid overall production — 25 touchdowns at 8.3 yards per attempt — and the guide's own upside scenario: if Reed improves and Elko lifts the defense into the elite tier, the market may be underrating Texas A&M.
Texas A&M Aggies.concerns: Turnover-worthy plays led the conference, and the intermediate middle throw is a specific, quantified weakness.
Texas A&M Aggies.scheme_fit: New play-caller Holmon Wiggins arrives, and the guide leaves open whether that aids his development.
Texas A&M Aggies.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 8.5 wins, argued as potential versus reality: Reed has not shown real progress in his weak areas and the defense is good but not among the SEC's elite. The guide is careful not to overstate the bear case, calling the Aggies capable of being very good while judging nine or more wins a challenge. It also sets out the market position — +850 to win the SEC, tied with Alabama, and 20-1 for the national championship.
Texas A&M Aggies.outlook_dependency: Very high. Reed's lack of progress is the first of the two reasons given for the Under, and his improvement is the first condition in the guide's upside scenario.

Texas Longhorns.career_experience: Established starter; PFF's eighth-best passer in the conference across the full 2025 season.
Texas Longhorns.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count; the guide isolates the last six games of 2025.
Texas Longhorns.passing: Last six games of 2025: 14 touchdowns at 7.8 yards per attempt. Across the full season he barely completed 60% and was PFF's eighth-best passer in the conference.
Texas Longhorns.rushing: Five rushing scores across the last six games.
Texas Longhorns.efficiency: Barely 60% completions on the season; 7.8 yards per attempt over the closing six games.
Texas Longhorns.turnovers: A 1.2% turnover-worthy play rate across the last six games.
Texas Longhorns.competition: None described — Manning is the settled starter.
Texas Longhorns.author_confidence: Conditional but constructive. The guide accepts many were disappointed by his season, then argues the closing form is the better guide, concluding that if he carries it forward the offense could be more explosive.
Texas Longhorns.positive_case: The closing six-game stretch — 14 touchdowns, 1.2% turnover-worthy play rate, 7.8 yards per attempt, five rushing scores, with Texas 5-1 straight up and 3-2-1 against the spread.
Texas Longhorns.concerns: Full-season accuracy barely above 60%, and heavy pressure — he was pressured on 35.6% of dropbacks, and his 165 pressured dropbacks led the SEC.
Texas Longhorns.supporting_cast: Improving. The team's biggest weakness, the offensive line, has been addressed: Sarkisian added bodies through the portal with Wake Forest right tackle Melvin Siani the standout, and returns left tackle Trevor Goosby and center Connor Robertson. The 2025 run game was limited at 4.2 yards per carry and 138 yards per game; the guide expects better protection and more push.
Texas Longhorns.portal_context: Offensive line reinforcements arrived via the portal, headlined by Melvin Siani from Wake Forest.
Texas Longhorns.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 9.5 wins, acknowledging Phil Steele ranks this the hardest schedule in the country. The guide concludes that if this is a genuine national title contender, ten wins should be attainable — and so should a national championship.
Texas Longhorns.outlook_dependency: High. The guide's explosiveness case is stated as conditional on Manning carrying his late-season form forward.

Vanderbilt Commodores.status: New starter — true freshman, described as the likely starter rather than a confirmed one.
Vanderbilt Commodores.career_experience: True freshman; five-star and the second-best prospect in his class per 247, with early projections making him a possible first-round pick.
Vanderbilt Commodores.rushing: Not a true dual threat, but the guide notes his running back background lets him extend plays and work as a designed runner.
Vanderbilt Commodores.competition: Open in the coach's telling — Lea says there will be a competition, while the guide judges Curtis the likely starter against Austin Peay.
Vanderbilt Commodores.author_confidence: Low, and stated directly. The guide's caution is that he is a true freshman in the SEC, and that equally talented quarterbacks have struggled in less demanding circumstances.
Vanderbilt Commodores.positive_case: A five-star, second-ranked in his class, projected by some as a possible first-round pick, with a running back background that helps him extend plays.
Vanderbilt Commodores.concerns: A true freshman in the SEC behind a wholly rebuilt offensive line, replacing a player who went 17-9, led Vanderbilt to its first 10-win season and finished second in Heisman voting.
Vanderbilt Commodores.supporting_cast: Weak up front. Four offensive line starters are gone and only one FBS transfer was added. Sedrick Alexander (5.5 per carry, 3.43 after contact) and Makhilyn Young (414 yards on 47 carries, 4.21 after contact) return, but with Diego Pavia's 862 rushing yards gone the guide expects a stark drop-off on the ground.
Vanderbilt Commodores.portal_context: Only one FBS offensive line transfer was added; on defense Lea added portal bodies including former four-star Ricardo Jones from Clemson.
Vanderbilt Commodores.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 5.5 wins. The guide explicitly acknowledges this may be an overly pessimistic reading, then lists why it holds: a freshman quarterback behind a wholly rebuilt line, and a secondary that could again be among the country's worst. It concludes that laying a price to reach six wins is not prudent.
Vanderbilt Commodores.outlook_dependency: Very high. The freshman quarterback is the first of the two reasons given for the Under, and the guide states plainly that decline, even for one season, is on the horizon.
Vanderbilt Commodores.conflicts: Lea is reported promising a competition while the guide simultaneously names Curtis the likely starter. Both are recorded; neither is resolved.
